aggressive_definition: Advanced prostate carcinoma, analyzed as the advanced category in localized versus advanced case subgroup analyses.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: Analyses were conducted for all prostate carcinoma cases together as well as for case subgroups (latent vs. nonlatent and localized vs. advanced).
study_design: Prospective cohort with a case-cohort analysis
cohort_total_n_excerpt: The cohort study consisted of 58,279 men ages 55-69 years at baseline in 1986.
reason: The prospective cohort analyzed all incident prostate carcinoma cases and separately analyzed localized versus advanced case subgroups, establishing both general and aggressive incident endpoints.

estimate_classifications.reason: The row has no numeric estimate and broadly labels omega-3 fatty acids, while the abstract reports null findings for the specific omega-3 fatty acids eicosapentaenoic acid and docosahexaenoic acid. It does not tie this row to an advanced-only result, so it is classified as general.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Oleic acid intake showed a nonsignificant positive association (RR = 1.38, 95% CI: 0.88-2.19).
estimate_classifications.reason: The reported RR is the overall prostate carcinoma estimate. The separate statement about subgroup analyses does not make this overall numeric estimate an aggressive estimate.

additional_estimates.comparison: Oleic acid intake in advanced prostate carcinoma subgroup analysis; contrast not specified in the abstract
additional_estimates.effect_excerpt: Analyses were conducted for all prostate carcinoma cases together as well as for case subgroups (latent vs. nonlatent and localized vs. advanced). No associations were found in multivariate analyses between prostate carcinoma and intake of energy, total fat, total saturated fatty acids, or total trans unsaturated fatty acids (RR highest vs. lowest quintile: 0.99, 1.10, 1.19, and 0.99, respectively). Oleic acid intake showed a nonsignificant positive association (RR = 1.38, 95% CI: 0.88-2.19). Positive associations were also observed for intake of oleic acid in subgroup analyses.
additional_estimates.count_excerpt: The cohort study consisted of 58,279 men ages 55-69 years at baseline in 1986.
additional_estimates.endpoint_definition: Advanced prostate carcinoma in the localized versus advanced case subgroup analysis
